speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It is a sensitive topic and we need to bear in mind that the nature of public discourse may affect the actions of others, especially among the young.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: There have been multiple initiatives introduced across agencies to raise awareness and build mental resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In addition, the National Council of Social Service's "Beyond the Label" movement addresses mental health stigma and promotes social inclusion for persons with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Peer support structures are also set up in all schools and Institutes of Higher Learning to help youth cope better with stress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We also recognise the important role that parents play in their children's mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: HPB rolled out a campaign in 2022 to help parents better understand their child's emotional health, identify early warning signs and provide support for their child.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We are making a major push to engage seniors who live alone, lack social support or are at-risk of social isolation through our Silver Generation Ambassadors and the network of Active Ageing Centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Assistance is also available in the community for individuals who are in psychological distress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Those requiring crisis support can access various crisis helplines, such as the Samaritans of Singapore Hotline and Care Text service and the Institute of Mental Health's Mental Health Helpline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: CareLine, a 24/7 social support hotline, also provides social support and emergency response services to seniors in distress and is operated by staff who can speak various dialects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-Being continues to review existing interventions and is working together to enhance the quality and accessibility of mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: At the same time, society plays a critical role in upholding a supportive social environment where there is little or no stigma against mental illness, where friends, family members and individuals feel safe to seek help, where parents work with schools to address their children's stress challenges and where everyone takes active steps to build up our mental well-being.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The first is, in relation to the people who died from suicide, was any analysis done on whether any of these people had sought assistance before that?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The second supplementary question is whether or not access to mental health should be made as easily accessible as access to general practitioners (GPs), where some are allowed to use the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) card and so on for such consultations.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As to Mr Vikram Nair's suggestion about improving access to counsellors and psychologists as well as the capabilities to the people they do access, indeed, that is part of the work that the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-Being is studying.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are a number of ways to do this.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: One is to find ways to reduce the barriers for people seeking help – some of that is stigma, some of that has to do with information, some of that is where the services are provided.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Another approach is to provide increased personnel in the locations where people perhaps might seek help so that there is more capability.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The third is to provide capability to other types of professionals where people are seeking assistance of another nature but where now they can continue to go on to seek mental health support as well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are exploring all of these as part of the work of the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-Being.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Motion for leave to bring in a Bill.
